output:
No. Build the S3 calls directly; keep them in one module.

The working directory here holds only the skill library and `CLAUDE.md` — no application code — so I scored this from your description rather than from your call sites. Assumption: ordinary S3 usage (put/get, maybe presigned URLs and multipart), one deployment target.

**What I found** — A `StorageProvider` interface with one implementation and no second vendor requested is speculative optionality, and the ledger says don't build it (the record calls this DROP). The deciding fact is your own: zero planned or requested second store, so the frequency and reach of the need it serves are both zero today.

**Why it matters** — Building it costs a port, an adapter, and an extra hop on every call path forever, and it taxes every future change: each new S3 capability you want (storage classes, presigned POST policies, multipart, object lock, event notifications, conditional writes) has to be threaded through the interface or leak around it. Not building it costs you almost nothing if a switch ever comes, *provided* the S3 SDK calls are confined to one module — then the migration is a mechanical rewrite of a known, small set of call sites, which is roughly the work you'd do anyway when the real second vendor exposes everything your guessed interface got wrong.

The portability argument is also weaker than it looks: interfaces designed before the second implementation exists are designed against an imagined vendor, and the parts that actually differ between object stores (consistency, auth, URL signing, lifecycle, error taxonomy) are exactly the parts that leak. Meanwhile the common case — R2, MinIO, GCS XML, Ceph — is S3-API-compatible, so the realistic "switch" is an endpoint and credentials change in config, which an interface does nothing to help.

**Do this first**
1. Check that S3 access is already localized rather than sprinkled: `rg -n "S3Client|boto3\.(client|resource)\(.s3|new S3|AmazonS3" --stats` — if the hits span more than one module, consolidate them into a single storage module with functions named for your domain (`storeUpload`, `getUploadUrl`), not for S3. That is locality, not an abstraction layer: no new interface, no adapter, no depth.
2. If you need to fake storage in tests, say so and solve that specific problem — an in-memory fake behind that one module, or LocalStack/MinIO in integration tests. Testability is a real requirement and is worth its own decision; it just isn't the vendor-portability argument.
3. Revisit if a second store is actually named in a plan, or an S3-incompatible target appears.

**What I did not check** — Your actual S3 call sites and how widely the client is imported (`rg` command above closes this). Whether a test-double need already exists that would justify the seam on different grounds (`rg -n "mock.*[Ss]3|moto|localstack|minio"`). Whether any contract or compliance obligation requires data-location portability — if one does, that's an external floor and changes the verdict.

```
Subject:        Proposed StorageProvider interface in front of the sole S3 client
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Pass
Necessity note: A vendor migration is not ruled out by any stated invariant, so this is
                not an impossible-state guard; it fails on worth, not on necessity.
V scores:       U=0  Nothing breaks today without it; S3 works.
                F=0  Vendor switches to date: zero; none scheduled.
                R=0  No user flow or environment encounters the need.
                I=1  If a switch happened, the alternative is a mechanical refactor of
                     localized call sites — cheap, and better informed by the real target.
C scores:       Subsystem-kinds Δ=+1 (port/adapter kind)  Dependency-edges Δ=+2
                Max-chain-depth Δ=+1  Subsystem-count Δ=+2
                M=1  Interface + adapter + their tests and docs to maintain.
                X=1  Lowest-common-denominator API pushes callers off S3-native features.
                E=2  Every future S3 capability must be threaded through the port or leak.
Confidence V:   High   (no second vendor planned or requested — stated directly)
Confidence C:   Medium (no code inspected; sketch-based deltas)
Outcome evidence: none
Decision:       DROP
Rationale:      Product value is zero on three of four axes because the anticipated
                variation does not exist, while cost is a permanent structural hop plus a
                real evolution tax. §8a grants an optionality premium only to a named,
                probable next feature; an unnamed hypothetical vendor fails YAGNI. DROP is
                fully reversible — the interface can be extracted later, against a real
                second implementation, with better information.
Next action:    Consolidate S3 SDK usage into one domain-named storage module if it is
                spread across files; introduce no interface.
Verification:   rg -n "S3Client|boto3\.(client|resource)\(.s3|new S3|AmazonS3" --stats
Minimal alt:    Locality without abstraction — single storage module, domain-named
                functions, S3 types not exported past its boundary.
Revisit when:   A second store is named in a plan or contract, an S3-incompatible target
                appears, or a test-double requirement is raised on its own merits.
```
